transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CISO, Ironbridge), Daniel Kim (SRE, Ironbridge), Arielle Tan (PM, Ironbridge)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for carving time for the weekly sync. we'll run through security items and any blockers for the pilot. samir is here for the deep bits. Marta, do you want to kick off with any updates from your side?
[00:22] Marta Ruiz: yeah thanks jordan. quick update, legal asked for the SOC two artifacts and also a narrative around audit logs, like where they live, retention and ability to export. we're also validating SSO flows for the infra team.
[00:35] Samir Desai: great, that's exactly what we expected. Jordan, i'll take the SAML and audit-log questions.
[00:42] Jordan Lee: perfect. on the SOC2, we can share our latest Type II report and the pen test summary, i'll drop those to the thread after the call.
[01:05] Daniel Kim: two quick asks — first, encryption at rest with customer KMS; second, we need to make sure audit logs include token-level mapping for requests, so we can correlate actions to users. is that supported now?
[01:22] Samir Desai: yes, we support envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS KMS or customer-managed keys. caveat: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can install the HSM/KMS connectors; for hosted we do bring-your-own-key via a KMS integration. on audit logs, we emit structured events — though the fields have changed a bit between runtimes, sorry if some of the earlier docs were confusing.
[01:50] Marta Ruiz: hmm ok, we saw in the last test that the logs truncated some request metadata; can we get a sample log export?
[02:05] Samir Desai: absolutely. i'll generate a sanitized sample log export — note, it may have some vendor names mangled by the export, our export pipeline anonymizes a few fields.
[02:18] Arielle Tan: timeline wise, legal wants confirmation of retention policy; we might need to show how deletion requests are handled end-to-end.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: we have an example retention config we can share. default for the pilot is 90 days for debug traces, 30 days for raw request logs unless you opt in for longer. samir, do we have flexible TTL per route?
[02:45] Samir Desai: yes, per-route TTLs are supported in config; you can set route-level retention, and we also have a deletion API to purge customer data on request. bear in mind, when you enable longer retention there is extra storage cost and audit throughput considerations.
[03:10] Daniel Kim: about SAML — we're trying to stage a test IdP. what's the fastest path to get SSO validated?
[03:22] Jordan Lee: best is you send the IdP metadata (SAML XML) and we'll load it into our staging environment. Samir will create a test org and a test user, then we can run login flows and token introspection.
[03:35] Samir Desai: i can provision the staging org today if you drop the metadata; small note — some fields for NameIDFormat need to be spcecified, we've seen mismatches (sic) in older IdPs.
[03:53] Marta Ruiz: noted. we'll get that over. also, compliance asked about cross-region data residency — can logs be stored only in eu-west for our EU customers?
[04:10] Samir Desai: for Private deployments yes, you can pin storage and compute to a region. for hosted, we have region controls but some aggregated telemetry is stored in a central analytics pipeline — we can export raw logs to your S3 in eu-west if that's a hard requirement.
[04:40] Arielle Tan: can you outline the exported log schema? we need field names to map to our SIEM.
[04:52] Samir Desai: i'll attach the schema as a json sample, but quick callout — we include fields: timestamp, org_id, route, user_id (if SSO), model, request_id, token_count, latency_ms, error_code. older runtime versions put model in model_name; there's some inconsistency, but we'll give a versioned schema.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: also to manage expectations, if you run the KV cache heavy benchmark we talked about, audit logs will generate significant volume — plan for about 2-3x the baseline log throughput during stress.
[05:45] Daniel Kim: that's why we need to run the 24h benchmark. can Redwood enable audit-logging at DEBUG level for that period without impacting performance?
[06:00] Samir Desai: yes, we can toggle log verbosity. recommendation: enable structured audit events but keep stack traces off unless needed; full DEBUG with stack traces will add a lot of payload.
[06:20] Marta Ruiz: on encryption, are you retaining unencrypted payloads anywhere? PII must never be logged in plaintext.
[06:33] Samir Desai: no, payloads are encrypted at rest. in-flight uses TLS. we also have scrubbers for a small set of PII by default, but for enterprise we recommend a tokenizer or pre-send redact step. note: scrubbing might affect model output quality if you remove context.
[06:58] Arielle Tan: legal also asked if you have an attestable deletion log for data deletion events — basically, an audit trail that shows deletion requests and completion timestamps.
[07:12] Samir Desai: yes, we emit a deletion event with a unique deletion_id and completion timestamp once purge has finished. we'll include that in the sample log export.
[07:35] Jordan Lee: quick open question — any blockers from your side that would stop the pilot this week?
[07:43] Marta Ruiz: blocking item is SOC2 artifacts; second is SAML idp metadata. once we have those we can move forward.
[07:55] Jordan Lee: ok action: i'll send SOC2 and pen test; Samir will send retention config and log schema. Daniel, you'll provide IdP metadata.
[08:12] Daniel Kim: yep, i'll aim to send metadata tomorrow. one more question: if we require customer-managed keys in hosted, is there an additional compliance review?
[08:25] Samir Desai: typically there is an additional step for key rotation and escrow details, but functionally it's supported. we have a short onboarding checklist for CMKs we can share.
[08:40] Marta Ruiz: for the SOC2 report, legal asked about any open exceptions or recent remediation tickets. can you surface that?
[08:51] Jordan Lee: we'll include an executive summary of exceptions and remediation status with the SOC2 package.
[09:05] Arielle Tan: regarding retention, we might need 7 years for certain transaction logs — is there a toggle to export to our cold storage?
[09:16] Samir Desai: yes, we have export hooks to S3/GCS. for long-term retention we recommend exporting parsimonious audit records to cold storage rather than keeping raw request payloads.
[09:35] Daniel Kim: good. last technical ask: can RBAC be scoped to teams inside the org so ops can't see prod prompts?
[09:46] Samir Desai: yes, RBAC supports role scopes and route-level permissions; we can lock down who can view request content, and provide redacted views for non-admins.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: do you want us to demo the RBAC config in the next ops sync?
[10:12] Marta Ruiz: yes, would be helpful.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: noted. we'll schedule that in the next week.
[10:30] Samir Desai: quick note about the retention API — if you request a purge, there's a window where cached artifacts (KV cache) may still serve responses for a short TTL unless you flush the cache. we can do immediate flush for a purge but that may cause brief latency spikes.
[10:55] Daniel Kim: understood. please document the flush behavior and expected latency impacts.
[11:05] Samir Desai: will do, i'll include it in the retention doc.
[11:20] Jordan Lee: any questions about the pilot data residency tests we planned?
[11:28] Arielle Tan: just confirmation that the staging org will mirror prod region for EU tests.
[11:35] Samir Desai: yes, we can provision staging in eu-west. small caveat, some telemetry aggregates still route to central analytics but raw logs can be stored in your region.
[11:55] Marta Ruiz: okay that's acceptable for now; legal will review the SOC2 artifacts.
[12:05] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps — i'll share SOC2 and summary; samir to share retention config, log schema, and sample export; daniel to share SAML metadata; we'll run the 24h benchmark next week with audit logging enabled. any final items?
[12:25] Daniel Kim: can we also get an example of how deletion events look in the logs?
[12:33] Samir Desai: yes, sample in the export.
[12:40] Jordan Lee: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a confirmation for the 24h benchmark slot.
[12:50] Marta Ruiz: thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings and small typos in product names; speaker labels near-perfect but some short crosstalk removed.
